answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks using Verifiable Delay Functions organized into a progressive difficulty terrace. Each identity requires sequential cryptographic proofs computed on an isolated hardware thread, forcing attackers to dedicate real silicon time and electricity per instance instead of multiplexing virtual clones. Stale proofs quickly become an inert relic. However, adversaries with custom ASIC hardware can compute proofs faster, creating hardware centralization.
